title: Are Threat Actors Preparing for and Exploiting AI Transformations?
subtitle: ACH across four sub-domains: AI-as-tool, AI-as-target, AI-transformed workflows, AI-relevant pre-positioning
analyticQuestion: Are threat actors deliberately preparing for and exploiting the enterprise transformation toward AI/agentic systems — and what does the actual evidence show about the scope, intent, and maturity of that activity, separated from vendor-narrative inflation and research-versus-in-the-wild misclassification?

keyJudgment.summary: Hypothesis is partially supported with sharp variation across four sub-domains. AI-as-tool is mature and confirmed; AI-as-target is observed but opportunistic, not strategic; AI-transformed workflows are exploitable and now seeing first in-the-wild attacks; deliberate state pre-positioning against AI orchestration layers remains inferred from trajectory, not documented in trace evidence.

subDomains.name: AI-as-tool
subDomains.definition: Attackers using LLMs and agents to conduct attacks against conventional targets
subDomains.maturityQuestion: How much of attacker tradecraft is now AI-accelerated?
subDomains.verdict: Confirmed, mature, observed in the wild

subDomains.name: AI-as-target
subDomains.definition: Attacks against AI infrastructure itself (supply chain on AI libs, model trojans, MCP server compromise)
subDomains.maturityQuestion: Are we seeing deliberate targeting of AI components?

subDomains.name: AI-transformed workflows as surface
subDomains.definition: Exploitation of enterprises because they've adopted AI (prompt injection in agents, RAG poisoning, indirect injection, agent privilege abuse)
subDomains.maturityQuestion: Is this in-the-wild or still mostly PoC?
subDomains.verdict: Real, first in-the-wild attacks now documented (postmark-mcp), most corpus still research

subDomains.name: AI-relevant pre-positioning
subDomains.definition: Long-horizon implant activity in environments that will host AI orchestration (Volt Typhoon-class staying-power against future AI-mediated effects)
subDomains.verdict: Inferred from doctrinal trajectory, not directly evidenced in public attribution

criminal.name: Criminal opportunistic exploitation of MCP infrastructure
criminal.markedBy: postmark-mcp incident (September 2025) — first publicly documented in-the-wild malicious MCP server

state.name: Deliberate state pre-positioning against AI orchestration layers
state.currentClosestEvidence: GTG-1002 (state actor uses MCP as orchestration platform, but targets are conventional)
state.watchSignature: Compromise of widely-used MCP server with payload structured for selective behavioral modification rather than broad credential harvesting

remainingGaps: Anthropic August 2025 primary report verification (currently read through secondary characterizations)
